subject: Is there a workaround to derive p values for pairwise CR coeffcient?

messages.author: 96a78639336ed702
messages.subject: Is there a workaround to derive p values for pairwise CR coeffcient?
parts:
Dear all,

The modularity.test function provides a single p value that represents significance of modularity, this is the case even when an object is divided into more than 2 partitions. When more than 2  partitions exist, while $CR.mat provides pairwise CRs among partitions, no corresponding p values or effect size z-scores are provided.

If there is any reason why they should not be calculated? If not, I may wish to see some workaround that allows for providing p values and z-scores for pairwise CRs.

Thank you.

Best regards,
Lv

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Is there a workaround to derive p values for pairwise CR coeffcient?
parts:
The original formulation of the CR tests (Adams 2016) stated that with more than 2 modules, the overall modularity is evaluated using the mean of the pairwise values (see pg. 568 column 1 at the bottom). The function in geomorph follows that procedure.

 

In theory tests of the pairwise CR could be obtained, along with their associated effect sizes. This would require extracting the CR matrix for each random permutation, and comparing all observed pairwise tests to their appropriate empirical sampling distribution. While this is not implemented automatically in geomorph at present, one could develop outside code that calls routines to do so.

 

Dean
